stem_tex: A particle moves along a line in such a way that its position at time $t$ is given by $s=t^3-9t^2+24t+5$. Its direction of motion changes when
explanation_tex: Differentiate: $v=s'=3t^2-18t+24=3(t-2)(t-4)$. Its sign changes at both $2$ and $4$, so the particle reverses at both times.

stem_tex: A body moves along a straight line so that its velocity $v$ at time $t$ is given by $v=6t^3+4t^2+7$. The distance the body covers from $t=0$ to $t=3$ equals
explanation_tex: Velocity is positive on $[0,3]$. The distance is $\int_0^3(6t^3+4t^2+7)\,dt=[\tfrac32t^4+\tfrac43t^3+7t]_0^3=178.5$.

stem_tex: A particle moves along a line with velocity $v=4t^2-8t$. The total distance traveled from $t=0$ to $t=4$ equals
explanation_tex: Velocity is negative on $(0,2)$ and positive on $(2,4)$. Thus distance is $-\int_0^2(4t^2-8t)\,dt+\int_2^4(4t^2-8t)\,dt=32$.

stem_tex: A particle moves along a line with velocity $v(t)=4t^2-8t$. The net change in position of the particle from $t=0$ to $t=4$ is
explanation_tex: Net displacement is the signed integral $[\tfrac43t^3-4t^2]_0^4=64/3$.

stem_tex: The acceleration of a particle moving on a straight line is given by $a=2\cos t$, and when $t=0$ the particle is at rest. The distance it covers from $t=0$ to $t=2$ is
explanation_tex: Integrating acceleration and using $v(0)=0$ gives $v=2\sin t$. This is nonnegative on $[0,2]$, so distance is $\int_0^2 2\sin t\,dt=2(1-\cos2)$.

stem_tex: During the worst 5-hour period of a hurricane the wind velocity, in miles per hour, is given by $v(t)=6t-t^2+120$, $0\leq t \leq 5$. The average wind velocity during this period (in mph) is
explanation_tex: Average velocity is $\frac15\int_0^5(6t-t^2+120)\,dt=120+15-25/3=126\tfrac23$ mph.

stem_tex: The acceleration of an object in motion is given by the vector $\vec{a}(t)=\langle 3t, e^{2t}\rangle$. If the object's initial velocity was $\vec{v}(0)=\langle 3,0\rangle$, which is the velocity vector at any time $t$?
explanation_tex: Integrate each acceleration component and apply the initial velocity: $v_x=3+3t^2/2$, $v_y=(e^{2t}-1)/2$.

stem_tex: A stone is thrown upward from the ground with an initial velocity of 120 ft/sec. Its average velocity (given that $a(t)=-32$ ft/sec$^2$) during the first 3 seconds is
explanation_tex: $v(t)=120-32t$, so its average is $\frac13\int_0^3(120-32t)\,dt=72$ ft/sec.

stem_tex: Assume that the density of vehicles (number of cars per mile) during morning rush hour, for the 30-mile stretch along a state highway southbound from a bridge, is given by $f(x)$, where $x$ is the distance, in miles, south of the bridge. Which of the following gives the number of vehicles (on this 30-mile stretch) from the bridge to a point $x$ miles south of the bridge?
choices_tex: $\displaystyle\sum_{k=1}^n f(x_k)\,\Delta x$ (where the 30-mile stretch has been partitioned into $n$ equal subintervals)
explanation_tex: Integrating density (cars per mile) over the road interval $[0,x]$ gives $\int_0^xf(t)\,dt$ cars.

stem_tex: The center of a city, that we will assume is circular, is on a straight highway (along the diameter of the circle). The radius of the city is 5 miles. The density of the population, in thousands of people per square mile, is given by $f(x)=15-3x$ at a distance $x$ miles from the highway. The population of the city (in thousands of people) is given by the integral
explanation_tex: At distance $x$ from the highway, each strip has length $2\sqrt{25-x^2}$. There are matching strips on both sides, so population is $4\int_0^5(15-3x)\sqrt{25-x^2}\,dx$ thousand.
source_correction: Corrected answer key to include strips on both sides of the highway.

stem_tex: A car accelerates from 0 to 90 mph in 12 seconds, with constant acceleration. (Note that 60 mph = 88 ft/sec, so 90 mph = 132 ft/sec.) The acceleration (in ft/sec$^2$) is
explanation_tex: Acceleration equals change in velocity divided by elapsed time: $a=132/12=11$ ft/sec$^2$.

stem_tex: A particle has velocity $\mathbf v(t)=\langle2t,t-2\rangle$ and initial position $(0,2)$. At time $t$ the position vector $\mathbf{R}$ is
explanation_tex: Integrate velocity from zero and add the initial position: $\mathbf R(t)=\langle t^2,t^2/2-2t+2\rangle$.

stem_tex: A particle has velocity $\mathbf v(t)=\langle2t,t-2\rangle$ and initial position $(0,2)$. The acceleration vector at time $t=3$ is
explanation_tex: Differentiate $\mathbf v(t)=\langle2t,t-2\rangle$: $\mathbf a(t)=\langle2,1\rangle$ for every $t$.

stem_tex: A particle has velocity $\mathbf v(t)=\langle2t,t-2\rangle$ and initial position $(0,2)$. The speed of the particle is at a minimum when $t$ equals
explanation_tex: Minimize squared speed $4t^2+(t-2)^2=5t^2-4t+4$. Its derivative is $10t-4$, so the minimum occurs at $t=2/5$.

stem_tex: A particle moves along a curve in such a way that its position vector and velocity vector are perpendicular at all times. If the particle passes through the point $(6,4)$, then the equation of the curve is
explanation_tex: Orthogonality gives $\mathbf R\cdot\mathbf R'=0$, hence $d(x^2+y^2)/dt=0$. The constant is $6^2+4^2=52$.

stem_tex: The velocity of an object is given by $\vec{v}(t)=\langle 4\sqrt{t}, 6\rangle$. If this object is at the origin when $t=1$, where was it at $t=0$?
explanation_tex: $\mathbf R(1)-\mathbf R(0)=\int_0^1\langle4\sqrt t,6\rangle\,dt=\langle8/3,6\rangle$. Since $\mathbf R(1)=0$, the initial position is $(-8/3,-6)$.

stem_tex: Suppose the current world population is 10 billion and the population $t$ years from now is estimated to be $P(t)=10e^{0.008t}$ billion people. On the basis of this supposition, the average population of the world, in billions, over the next 30 years will be approximately
explanation_tex: The average is $\frac1{30}\int_0^{30}10e^{0.008t}\,dt=\frac{10}{0.24}(e^{0.24}-1)\approx11.302$ billion.

stem_tex: A beach opens at 8 A.M.\ and people arrive at a rate of $R(t)=15+50t$ people per hour, where $t$ represents the number of hours the beach has been open. Assuming no one leaves before noon, at what time will there be 130 people there?
explanation_tex: The accumulated arrivals are $\int_0^t(15+50u)\,du=15t+25t^2$. Setting this equal to $130$ gives $t=2$, or 10 A.M.

stem_tex: Suppose the amount of a drug in a patient's bloodstream $t$ hours after intravenous administration is $A(t)=\dfrac{45}{(t+1)^2}$ mg. The average amount in the bloodstream during the first 5 hours is
explanation_tex: The average amount is $\frac15\int_0^5\frac{45}{(t+1)^2}\,dt=9[-1/(t+1)]_0^5=7.5$ mg.

stem_tex: A rumor spreads through a town at the rate of $R(t)=t^2+15t$ new people per day $t$ days after it was first heard. Approximately how many people hear the rumor during the third week (from the 14th to the 21st days) after it was first heard?
explanation_tex: Integrate the rate over the third week: $[t^3/3+15t^2/2]_{14}^{21}=4009.833\ldots$, approximately $4010$ people.

stem_tex: Oil is leaking from a tanker at the rate of $L(t)=1500e^{-0.4t}$ gal/hr, where $t$ is given in hours. The total number of gallons of oil that will leak out during the first 6 hours is approximately

Population density depends on distance $x$ from the city center according to $\begin{array}{c|rrrrrr}x\text{ (miles)}&0&3&6&9&12&15\\\hline f(x)\text{ (hundreds per square mile)}&60&50&42&30&18&8\end{array}$. Using the five width3 intervals in the table, apply a left Riemann sum to $100\int_0^{15}2\pi x f(x)\,dx$ to estimate the population, rounded to the nearest person.
explanation_tex: A thin annulus has area $2\pi x\,dx$, so population is $100\int_0^{15}2\pi x f(x)\,dx$. With width3 and left endpoints0,3,6,9,12, the estimate is $600\pi[0(60)+3(50)+6(42)+9(30)+12(18)]=532800\pi\approx1{,}673{,}841$ people.

stem_tex: If a factory continuously dumps pollutants into a river at the rate of $p(t)=\dfrac{\sqrt{t}}{240}$ tons per day, then the amount dumped after 9 weeks is approximately
explanation_tex: Nine weeks is $63$ days. The amount is $\int_0^{63}\sqrt t/240\,dt=63^{3/2}/360\approx1.389$ tons.

stem_tex: A roast at $180^\circ$F is put into a refrigerator whose temperature is $45^\circ$F. The temperature of the roast is cooling at time $t$ at the rate of $R(t)=-10e^{-0.1t}\,{}^\circ$F per minute. The temperature, to the nearest degree F, of the roast 25 minutes after it is put into the refrigerator is
explanation_tex: Initial temperature plus accumulated cooling gives $T(25)=180+\int_0^{25}-10e^{-0.1t}\,dt=80+100e^{-2.5}\approx88.208^\circ$F, rounding to $88^\circ$F.

stem_tex: How long will it take to release 9 tons of pollutant if the rate at which the pollutant is being released is $P(t)=te^{-0.25t}$ tons per week?
explanation_tex: Solve $\int_0^Tte^{-t/4}\,dt=16[1-(1+T/4)e^{-T/4}]=9$. Numerical solution gives $T\approx7.547$ weeks, closest to $7.5$.

stem_tex: What is the total area bounded by the curve $f(x)=x^3-5x^2+4x$ and the $x$-axis on the interval $0\leq x \leq 4$?
explanation_tex: Factor $f=x(x-1)(x-4)$, positive on $(0,1)$ and negative on $(1,4)$. Thus area is $\int_0^1f(x)\,dx-\int_1^4f(x)\,dx=71/6$.

stem_tex: A tank has signed outward flow rate $W(t)=-0.15t^2-0.4t+3$ gal/hr, where negative values represent inflow. What is the net water loss, in gallons, over $0\le t\le4$?
explanation_tex: Net loss is the signed integral $\int_0^4(-0.15t^2-0.4t+3)\,dt=[-0.05t^3-0.2t^2+3t]_0^4=5.6$ gallons. The rate becomes negative after $t=10/3$, representing inflow during that part of the interval, which reduces the net loss.

source_original.stem_tex: Water is leaking from a tank at the rate of $W(t)=-0.15t^2-0.4t+3$ gal/hr. The total amount, in gallons, that will leak out in the next 4 hours is approximately

stem_tex: A bacterial culture is growing at the rate of $B(t)=1500e^{0.04t}$ bacteria in $t$ hours. The total increase in bacterial population during the second hour is approximately
explanation_tex: The second hour is $1\le t\le2$. The increase is $\int_1^2 1500e^{0.04t}\,dt=37500(e^{0.08}-e^{0.04})\approx1592.861$, about $1593$ bacteria.

stem_tex: A website opens at noon. Its rate $R(t)$ in visitors/hour increases as shown in the graph, where $t$ is hours after noon. Each vertical grid interval represents one hour, from $t=0$ to $t=8$. Use a midpoint or trapezoidal sum to approximate when the 400th visitor arrives.
explanation_tex: From the graph, hourly rates through 5 P.M. are approximately $0,15,59,123,200,277$. Trapezoids give about $297$ visitors by 4 P.M. and $535.5$ by 5 P.M.; therefore the 400th visitor arrives between 4 and 5 P.M.

figure.alt: Source rate graph; vertical grid lines are hours 0 through 8.

stem_tex: The velocity table is $\begin{array}{c|rrrrrr}t\text{ (sec)}&0&2&4&6&8&10\\\hline v(t)\text{ (units/sec)}&4&5&2&-2&-4&0\end{array}$. Use the five indicated trapezoids to estimate how far from its starting point the object is when it comes to rest at $t=10$.
explanation_tex: Each interval has width $2$. The trapezoidal displacement is $(4+5)+(5+2)+(2-2)+(-2-4)+(-4+0)=6$. The object is about $6$ units from its starting point.

stem_tex: An 18-wheeler is traveling at a speed given by $v(t)=\dfrac{100(t+1)}{t+2}$ mph at time $t$ hours. The fuel economy for the diesel fuel in the truck is given by $f(v)=5+0.008v$ miles per gallon. The amount, in gallons, of diesel fuel used during the first 3 hours is approximately
explanation_tex: Fuel use per hour is speed divided by fuel economy. Thus $G=\int_0^3\frac{100(t+1)/(t+2)}{5+0.008[100(t+1)/(t+2)]}\,dt\approx37.459$ gallons, closest to $37.5$.
